game: IND @ LAC Week 7 2025, kickoff 2025-10-19 16:05 ET, roof dome, LAC -2.5, total 48.5

script.base: Close dome game, not a blowout and not a slog. LAC is only -2.5 with implied totals LAC 25.5 and IND 23.0 off a 48.5 total, so both offenses stay live. LAC leads by a field goal at half or late, Herbert stays balanced to Keenan Allen (23 targets, 122 yards weeks 4-6), Ladd McConkey (22/150) and Quentin Johnston (17/138), and the Hampton/Vidal committee splits carries (24 and 22) without a 25-carry grind. IND stays on schedule through Jonathan Taylor (55 carries, 265 rush yards in that window) and, with Josh Downs out, a redistributed pass game to Tyler Warren and Michael Pittman rather than an abandon-the-run script.
script.flip1: LAC jumps ahead by two scores. IND is missing CB Charvarius Ward (out, concussion) and Kenny Moore II is questionable, and IND has already allowed 18 passes of 20+ for 235 yards, so Herbert's explosives script takes over. Taylor's carries stall the way a trailing dog's back stalls, and LAC runs clock late with Omarion Hampton and Kimani Vidal.
script.flip2: Taylor hits the soft LAC run front early (5.07 YPC, 25 runs of 10+ in 6 games) and IND controls the clock. LAC falls behind, the committee run dies, and Herbert is forced into more dropbacks behind a compromised line (Joe Alt doubtful, Trey Pipkins out, Jamaree Salyer questionable).

injury_fallout: Source is the pre-game nflverse injury report; final inactives (~90 minutes before kick) are not in the pack, so every Questionable tag is unresolved. IND: Josh Downs out (concussion) vacates 20 targets / 120 yards / 112 air yards from weeks 4-6; Ashton Dulin out (chest) vacates 6/66/107. That volume should split toward Tyler Warren (already 19/177/147), Michael Pittman (19/100/208) and checkdowns to Taylor (13/54), not a single named heir. Tyler Goodson out (groin) removes a spare RB; DJ Giddens was only 5 carries / 22 yards in that window, so Taylor's 55-carry share holds or ticks up, it does not create a committee. Charvarius Ward out and Kenny Moore II questionable (Achilles) weaken IND's secondary and help LAC pass-catchers if Moore sits, especially slot/intermediate. LAC: Joe Alt doubtful (ankle), Trey Pipkins out (knee) and Jamaree Salyer questionable (knee) raise pressure risk, which cuts deep WR yards and pushes quick throws to Allen, McConkey and the RBs. Khalil Mack questionable (elbow) is the swing for IND's run efficiency. Hassan Haskins questionable (chest) would only move his 11/27 onto Hampton and Vidal. Elijah Molden doubtful (thumb) plus LBs Denzel Perryman and Troy Dye questionable thin the middle, which is Warren's area. Derius Davis questionable is a gadget WR not in the week 4-6 target list.

matchup.shell: No MOFO/MOFC or man/zone charting saved. Inference only from location splits: LAC blitzes just 24% and allows 8.85 YPA on 39 middle attempts versus 5.06 YPA on 81 right-side attempts and 6.14 on 65 left-side attempts, so the soft area is the middle, not the outside corner. IND blitzes 32% and allows 8.35 YPA on 80 left-side attempts versus 5.45 on 101 right-side attempts.
matchup.pressure: LAC blitz rate 24%. IND EPA/dropback is 0.19 versus the blitz and 0.30 with no blitz, so Indianapolis is better on the more common unblitzed look. IND blitz rate 32%. LAC EPA/dropback is 0.14 versus the blitz and -0.02 with no blitz, so Herbert has been better when blitzed, but that split is at risk with Alt doubtful, Pipkins out and Salyer questionable. Mack questionable means IND may not face LAC's best rusher.
matchup.bleeds: LAC bleeds the run (5.07 YPC, 25 runs of 10+ over 6 games) and the middle of the field (8.85 YPA). LAC is not an explosive-pass pushover (14 passes of 20+ for 201 yards). IND bleeds explosives (18 of 20+ for 235 yards) and the left side (8.35 YPA) while holding the run better (4.39 YPC, 16 runs of 10+).
matchup.overlap: Taylor is the primary rusher into the exact spot LAC gives up (5.07 YPC and explosive runs), with Goodson out and Perryman/Dye questionable. Warren is the most efficient IND pass-catcher in the window (177 yards on 19 targets, 9.3 yards per target, 147 air yards) into that same middle, and Downs' 20 targets are now vacant. Johnston into IND's explosive allowance plus Ward out is a real overlap, but LAC's tackle injuries cut against chasing deep yards, so that overlap is not a leg.

form: Using the week 3-6 logs, not a season average, as the decider. Taylor rush yards 102, 76, 66, 123; weeks 4-6 sum to the listed 265 (88.3 per game, 4.82 YPC) on 55 carries against Giddens 5/22, Daniel Jones 4/24 and Ameer Abdullah 3/13. Two of those four games cleared 89.5 and two did not. Warren receiving 38, 70, 44, 63; weeks 4-6 sum to 177 (59.0 per game) and only the 70 cleared 66.5. Pittman 73, 41, 39, 20 is trending down (100 yards on 19 targets and 208 air yards, 5.3 yards per target), so he is not the overlap play despite Downs being out. Allen 65, 37, 58, 27 is also trending down (122 yards on 23 targets). McConkey weeks 4-6 were 11, 39, 100, a spike not a trend. Vidal's prop log is only two games (18 and 124 rush yards), which sum to the listed 142, so a 71.5 line is that two-game median, not a mispriced 47-yard role. Hampton's yard log (24, 70, 128, 44) does not reconcile to the listed 172 rush yards, so he is not used as a leg. Pierce's listed week 4-6 line (4 targets, 48 yards) conflicts with last-four yards 36, 68, 67, 48, so no Pierce leg. No similar-defense charting beyond these splits.

The dog (IND) should throw slightly more; the leader (LAC) runs late, but the margin is too small for a 25-carry grind. Usage from shares, not raw averages: Taylor had 55 of IND's listed RB carries in weeks 4-6; LAC's backfield was Hampton 24 / Vidal 22 / Haskins 11.

data_check.notes: No projection, no sims, no Pinnacle, no two-sided prices. Stand-in lines are 2025 season-to-date medians, so model_p values are hand estimates from role and matchup, not 3-sim probabilities, and both sit under the 70% suspicion line. Taylor: last-four mean 91.75 agrees slightly with over 89.5, weeks 4-6 mean 88.3 disagrees slightly, hit rate 2 of 4. Mixed, not a clean disagree, so the strong matchup read is flagged for the human rather than cut. Warren: last-four hit rate 1 of 4 and a 59.0 recent mean disagree with over 66.5. That is a real disagree on a strong read (Downs' 20 targets vacated, 9.3 yards per target, middle 8.85 YPA), so it is flagged, not cut. A lean with that disagree would have been dropped. No price means nothing can be sized. Vidal under 71.5 was considered and passed: 18 and 124 sum to the listed 142, so 71.5 is his two-game median, not a soft number. Hampton and Pierce logs do not reconcile and were not used.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and this lost because the counter-case was live. Perryman, Dye and Mack all played, LAC loaded the box, IND fell behind and Taylor finished with a 14-carry, mid-60s day like the 76 and 66 already on his log, so 89.5 never had the matchup upgrade. On Warren, Pittman took the first look at Downs' targets, the middle 8.85 YPA did not show up in this game, and Warren posted another 44- or 63-yard line while 66.5, already his season median and above his 59-yard recent mean, was the tax. The redistribution might also have been only one extra target, which is not enough. If that counter is judged stronger than the read, both legs should be cut; they are flagged here because the pre-kick read is still the stronger side and the missing no-vig cannot settle it.
slip_story: One base-script stack only: competitive dome game, IND moves the ball without a blowout. Taylor rush over is the soft-front, bellcow piece; Warren receiving over is the Downs-vacancy piece into LAC's middle. They can win together in the one-score script. Do not add LAC WR overs or a game over, which need the IND-trails flip that kills Taylor. Do not add a total under. No TD legs, no second market on either player, two legs max. Vidal, Hampton, Allen, McConkey, Johnston, Pittman, Pierce and Giddens are not on the slip.
